verified_by: TrueJoyBirthing research (official SC DHEC / DPH sources)

out_of_hospital_midwife.kit_ordering: Out-of-hospital providers (midwives, physicians) order newborn screening filter-paper cards and tubes from the SC Public Health Laboratory. Supplies are requested via the DPH Newborn Screening supply ordering process / program forms page.
out_of_hospital_midwife.submission_deadline: Blood specimen collected 24-48 hours of age; repeat screen required at 2 weeks of age if first collected before 24 hours.
out_of_hospital_midwife.specimen_tracking: Results returned to the ordering provider; parents receive results from their provider. Tracking via the SC DPH Newborn Screening portal.

metabolic_screening.state_form_note: South Carolina provides an official state refusal form, DPH 1804. Under S.C. Code § 44-37-30(C), newborn screening may be refused only on religious grounds; the signed DPH 1804 is filed with the provider and the SC Department of Public Health.
metabolic_screening.statute: S.C. Code § 44-37-30(C) (newborn screening; religious exemption); S.C. Code § 44-37-20 (eye prophylaxis); S.C. Code § 44-37-70 (CCHD)

hearing_screening.program_name: South Carolina Early Hearing Detection and Intervention (EHDI)
hearing_screening.out_of_hospital_path: For home/birth-center births, the midwife performs or arranges the newborn hearing screen and documents results; refusal is documented on the screening paperwork / medical record per S.C. Code 44-37-30.
hearing_screening.statute: S.C. Code § 44-37-30 (includes hearing screening); SC EHDI 1-3-6 benchmarks

cchd_screening.out_of_hospital_performer: The attending midwife or physician performs pulse oximetry (CCHD) in the out-of-hospital setting and documents it; refusal documented per S.C. Code 44-37-30/44-37-70.
cchd_screening.statute: S.C. Code § 44-37-70 (critical congenital heart defect screening)

erythromycin_eye_ointment.waiver: Prophylactic eye treatment (0.5% erythromycin) must be instilled into each eye within one hour of birth; a parent may object on religious grounds and the refusal is documented in the medical record. South Carolina issues no separate standalone waiver form beyond the documented refusal.
erythromycin_eye_ointment.note: Mandatory instillation within one hour of birth to prevent ophthalmia neonatorum.

vitamin_k.note: South Carolina does not mandate vitamin K; parental choice of oral, intramuscular shot, or decline, documented in the birth record.

hepatitis_b_vaccine.note: Birth dose reported to SIMON by birthing facilities; infants born to HBsAg-positive mothers are referred for Hepatitis B case management.

gestational_diabetes.midwife_role: Licensed midwives in South Carolina provide gestational diabetes screening/counseling in prenatal care and refer for diagnostic testing when indicated.
gestational_diabetes.note: Prenatal informed-choice item; no state newborn-screening form.

group_b_strep.midwife_role: Licensed midwives offer GBS screening in late pregnancy and arrange intrapartum prophylaxis per protocol for out-of-hospital births when indicated.
group_b_strep.note: Prenatal informed-choice item; no state newborn-screening form.

program_contact.name: SC Department of Public Health  Newborn Screening Program
